title: Survey Corner
primary_metric: angular deviation (degrees) between a candidate pin's actual corner angle and the plat's expected corner angle -- lower deviation wins

options.A: Recommend Pin 1 -- the older, weathered monument -- as the true SW corner
options.B: Recommend Pin 2 -- the newer monument -- as the true SW corner

sources.claim: Real NGS survey monument "D 565," PID QX0584, Gardiner MT -- coordinates and elevation
sources.title: NGS Data Sheet -- PID QX0584 ("D 565")

_ext: keys below are pipeline extensions, additive to SPEC section 4

cohort_bands.note: Two clean triangles and one parallel-line derivation is enough load for a small room; run D1-D3 as a whole-group derivation before splitting into pairs for D4-D5.

Split into two teams, one per candidate pin, each independently working D2-D6 for their pin before the room reconciles at D7 -- surfaces the trap (pin age vs. angle math) as a live disagreement instead of a lecture.

deliverables.text: The plat's expected corner angle from Appendix B's parallel-lines-and-transversal setup.
Pin 1's actual corner angle from Appendix C's total-station reading.
Pin 2's actual corner angle from Appendix C's total-station reading.
The Pin 1 witness triangle's third angle and its classification.
The Pin 2 witness triangle's third angle and its classification.
The angular deviation of each pin's actual angle from the plat's expected angle.
The percentage-margin verdict between the two deviations and a recommendation.

appendices.title: How To Math Questions To Research

balance.argument_a: Pin 1's measured distance from the NW corner (247.8 ft) is only 2.8 ft off the plat's recorded 245.0 ft boundary length, beating Pin 2's 6.5 ft distance deviation -- a real, quantified distance-based match, on top of Pin 1 being the physically older monument.
balance.argument_b: Pin 2's actual corner angle is 91.0 degrees, only 4.0 degrees off the plat's expected 87 degrees -- closer than Pin 1's 4.5-degree deviation -- and its witness triangle comes out acute, a cleaner check than Pin 1's obtuse triangle.
balance.margin_basis: Absolute angular deviation (degrees) between each candidate pin's actual corner angle and the plat's expected angle, computed in cases/survey-corner/sensitivity_model.py from Appendix B/C figures. Lower deviation wins.

modeling_assumptions.text: Northwest corner plat-recorded angle (93 degrees, i.e. 3 degrees past square) carries real historic recording/transcription uncertainty from the original 1962 survey, scaled against the 3-degree excess-past-square rather than the full 93-degree angle -- the excess is the part a real deed recording error would actually land on.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Flexed +/-50% on the 3-degree excess (1.5-4.5 degrees, i.e. NW angle 91.5-94.5 degrees) in Tier 2 probe 5; winner (Pin 2) does not flip across the swept range, margin ranges 8.33%-16.67%.

modeling_assumptions.text: Pin 1/Pin 2 field readings and witness-tie triangle angles are Priya's own authored field survey for this dispute -- no public database of real property-line disputes' raw field books exists.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Not FLEX-swept (authored field data, not a stated numeric assumption).
